newsitem.title: CHINA: China exchange presidents welcome stock crackdown.
newsitem.headline: China exchange presidents welcome stock crackdown.

text.p: The heads of China's two stock exchanges on Wednesday welcomed Beijing's crackdown on share trading, saying the markets needed stability to develop, the China Securities newspaper said.
A harshly worded commentary in the People's Daily on Monday said that China's stock markets were overheated and warned that if there were a crash, Beijing would not step in to help investors.

"The commentary was aimed at curbing excessive speculation, standardising market activity and protecting the interests of investors," Yan Xianghai, president of the Shanghai Stock Exchange, was quoted by the newspaper as saying.

"The securities markets are a high-risk business and can only be developed with the precondition of stability," the newspaper quoted Zhuang Xinyi, the Shenzhen bourse president, as saying in a companion article.
Shanghai's Yang said that despite the crackdown, China's stock markets would continue to develop, with standardisation the key.
"The basic principle of developing the markets will not be changed," Yang said. "Investors must take a long-term view and not blindly buy when prices rise and sell when prices fall."

Shenzhen's Zhuang said blue-chip stocks had led the surge in China's stock rises this year and that after the crackdown, the blue chips had fallen less than stocks of poorly performing companies, indicating that correct investment choices could reduce risk.
The two presidents said that the exchanges would shortly draw up plans for next year and that they would hold to a dual policy of standardisation and development, the newspaper said.
